decisions.statement: Every page of that page type is answered in this one answer.
The pages taken away are the pages the index names of that page type.
A count says the most pages one run of this change takes away.
A count left out takes away every page of that page type.
A count below the pages there are takes the first the index names.
A page type the index does not name is refused.
A page type no page is of is refused rather than answered as no edit.
The page stating the page type is no page of that type and remains.
A page and every file that page keeps beside the page go together.
Which files sit beside a page is read from the index rather than from the folder.
A file the page claims and the tree has no body at is left alone.
The files beside a page go before that page's own file.
Every entry in a parent's `parts` is dropped before any file goes.
A parent naming a page bare rather than qualified is dropped just the same.
A parent naming two pages that go loses both entries by one edit over it.
One page refused refuses the whole change, and the refusal names that page.
Every file goes in this one answer, so no reading comes between two removals.
Nothing here reads a page's own body to find the files beside it.

definition: every page of one page type taken away, each with the files beside it
